tasks.title: Back-flow acceptance criteria ac1..ac9 into the Story
tasks.summary: The Story ships with acceptanceCriteria: [], so the nine criterionId values ac1..ac9 that the LLD test-strategy acceptanceMapping is organized around are unanchored forward-declarations — the mapping cannot be audited at review or approve time. Write the nine criteria into the Story with explicit text, using the set the LLD already makes inferable: ac1 catalog keys absent from the on-disk config are filled with catalog defaults; ac2 present-and-type-valid keys are carried through untouched; ac3 present-but-type-invalid keys are repaired to the catalog default; ac4 catalog-unenumerable namespaces (models.analyze.roleTiers, models.analyze.byRepo, models.agents) survive blindly; ac5 reconcile is idempotent and writes at most once, only when changed; ac6 maintenance.update runs the reconcile after the build step and reports it additively via MaintenanceResult; ac7 daemon boot runs the reconcile unconditionally and never aborts boot on failure; ac8 the catalog is relocated into src/config with no daemon→cli import edge; ac9 read/parse/write failures abort without writing and are surfaced as structured non-fatal outcomes. Cross-reference each criterion to the tasks that discharge it. No production code is touched.

tasks.title: Implement the pure reconcileConfig module with a named catalog-error type
tasks.summary: Add src/config/reconcile.ts exporting `ConfigReconcileResult { config, changed, carried, filled, repaired }` and `reconcileConfig(existing: unknown, catalog: readonly ConfigOption[] = CONFIG_CATALOG): ConfigReconcileResult`. Strictly pure — no fs, IPC, socket or clock — because the daemon-boot caller runs before the socket exists (src/daemon/index.ts:178, DB opens only at :213). Build the output as a MERGE over a deep clone of `existing`, never a rebuild from catalog rows, so catalog-unenumerable keys survive blindly. Own the dot-path get/set walk inside this module (no reusable helper exists); mirror the ancestor-collision rule already inlined in the config.write handler at src/daemon/index.ts:1137-1139, strengthened with `!Array.isArray(...)` in the plain-object predicate, and record the discarded scalar in the repair record so callers can name the loss. The type-match predicate is a 4-arm exhaustive switch over the confirmed closed union 'string'|'number'|'boolean'|'enum'; note explicitly in a comment that 'enum' rows carry no allowed-values field so their predicate degenerates to `typeof === 'string'` (7 of 41 rows). Existence is tested with hasOwnProperty, never truthiness; null is rejected for object/string rows. Settling open question s8-cd3: the two catalog-integrity failures — a catalog row with an out-of-domain `type`, and a catalog row whose own default fails its own predicate — throw a dedicated exported `ConfigCatalogError extends Error` carrying the offending catalog path, distinct from every I/O and parse failure, so downstream callers can report a programmer error in our shipped catalog differently from a user-config or filesystem error. `carried`/`filled`/`repaired` carry dot-paths (repairs also carry the discarded value) so callers can log per-key detail. Derive `changed` from the same comparison that built the document. Land it unwired and inert.

tasks.title: Implement the shared read/reconcile/write-once I/O wrapper and record the two LLD deviations
tasks.summary: Add the I/O side alongside the pure reconciler in src/config (a plain module function, NOT a ConfigStore method — src/config/store.ts is a deprecated LMDB row store with no fs access at all and is not the config.json owner, so the a3 wrapper resolves to no). It resolves the file through PATHS.config from src/shared/paths.js; reads the whole document once; stats mtimeMs+size at read time; calls reconcileConfig; and writes at most once and only when `changed`, via write-temp-then-rename after re-statting to detect concurrent modification. The write unit is defined precisely: exactly one writeFile targeting the temp config document plus one rename per reconcile that reports changed, and zero of both when changed is false. Error paths: ENOENT degrades to reconcileConfig(undefined); any other read errno aborts with the errno reported and nothing written; a JSON SyntaxError aborts with message plus byte offset and explicitly does NOT fall back to the undefined path (default-filling over a corrupt document would destroy the dynamic namespaces); a ConfigCatalogError propagates as a distinct structured outcome kind so callers can flag a shipped-catalog bug rather than a user-config problem; a write failure unlinks the temp file; a concurrent-modification detection abandons the write. Every failure is returned as a structured non-fatal outcome, never thrown at the caller. Ship a deviation note as a deliverable — a comment block at the wrapper (and mirrored in the Story/LLD amendment) recording (a) that `globalConfigDirs` returns [templates, feedback, conventions] and is NOT the config.json resolver, so PATHS.config supersedes the LLD contract entry `globalConfigDirs` and invariant c7, with the evidence (src/daemon/index.ts:179/1118/1129/1144), and (b) the open question s8-sbdry3 deviation: the CLI update path writes ~/.insrc/config.json directly, in tension with the daemon-owns-on-disk-state rule, why alternative a4 was rejected, and that the approver must confirm it.

tasks.title: Settle the stale-catalog hazard and ship a standalone built-catalog loader
tasks.summary: Settle and implement the one genuinely open design decision, as an independently testable unit ahead of any update wiring: maintenance.update runs inside a CLI process holding the PRE-update CONFIG_CATALOG in its module graph, while `npm run build` at src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:106-112 rewrites out/ underneath it — so an in-process reconcile against the resident module is a no-op for exactly the shape change this Story targets, and is indistinguishable from 'already normalized'. Resolution (a) is chosen: load the freshly built catalog module via `await import()` of the build output and pass it as reconcileConfig's injectable `catalog` argument; on import rejection fall back to (b) — report only and defer the authoritative reconcile to the next daemon boot (landed in t9), never claiming a confident no-change against the stale in-memory catalog. Deliver this as a standalone helper `loadBuiltCatalog(): Promise<readonly ConfigOption[] | null>` in src/config that returns the freshly imported catalog or null on import rejection, with unit tests against a built-catalog fixture directory and a missing-output case. Record the decision and its rationale in a doc comment on the helper; the call-site wiring and its rationale comment land in t12.

tasks.title: Wire the reconcile into maintenance.update after the build step
tasks.summary: Insert the reconcile between src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:112 and :114 — strictly after git fetch/merge and `npm run build`, never before — using the t7 wrapper and the t10 `loadBuiltCatalog` resolution (fall back to defer-to-boot and report the deferral when it returns null). It must run unconditionally (no opt-in flag) and write at most once, only when changed. Because every failure path in update() early-returns `ok: false` (L55/65/75/84/88/99/109) and the whole body sits in one try/catch returning ok:false (L116-118), the non-fatal requirement needs its OWN inner try/catch — a naive throw would flip a successful update to failed. On success populate configReconcile with counts and push 'reconcile' onto the existing `steps` channel; on failure capture the message into configReconcile.error while still returning ok:true, and report a ConfigCatalogError distinguishably (an explicit shipped-catalog-bug message, not an anonymous failure string) so it is not flattened into the same channel as a user-config or I/O failure. onLog carries the per-key detail the LLD requires, not just counts: emit exactly one reconcile summary line plus one detail line per filled and per repaired key naming its catalog dot-path, and for an ancestor collision the detail line also names the discarded scalar value so the loss is stated, not hidden. An explicit no-change line or an explicit failure line is emitted when there is nothing filled or repaired — never silence — and onLog is the only progress channel. Add the rationale comment for the stale-catalog resolution at this call site, and an acceptance-visible pointer to the t7 deviation note covering s8-sbdry3 (the CLI writing ~/.insrc/config.json directly). Ship the update integration tests (stubbed git/build steps, recording onLog collector) alongside.
